 Flyers coach Rick Tocchet has tough decisions to make on youngsters when veterans return

 X 
 The Flyers have several prospects, including Oliver Bonk, who they feel are developing ahead of schedule. (AP Photo/Matt Slocum) 
 By Wayne Fish | flyingfishhockey.com PUBLISHED: October 24, 2026 at 11:07 AM EDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... It’s a pleasant problem to have.
 That is, the potential overcrowding of the Flyers’ roster when some of the veteran players come off injured reserve.
 To say the play of youngsters such as Cole Knuble, Jacob Gaucher and defensemen Oliver Bonk and Hunter McDonald has been inspiring would probably be an understatement.
 All Knuble did was score his first two NHL goals during a 3-1 win at Buffalo on Wednesday night in just his second game with the Flyers.
 In the same game, Bonk contributed two assists and McDonald played a part in holding the Sabres to that single goal.
 On Friday, both injured defensemen Rasmus Ristolainen and Cam York skated in practice. It’s a safe bet that Ristolainen will be back in action soon and York can’t be too far behind. The status of forwards Travis Konecny and Owen Tippett are a little more uncertain.
 As the veterans do return, coach Rick Tocchet is going to have some tough decisions to make.
 Has Bonk played well enough at both ends of the rink to warrant a longer trial run in the starting lineup? If he sticks around, who goes to the bench? The Flyers already have been rotating David Jiricek and Simon Benoit in and out of the lineup. Now both could be sitting a while.
 Should Knuble continue to show prowess at both ends of the rink, it might be difficult to send him back to the Lehigh Valley Phantoms.
 Like previously mentioned, this is not necessarily a bad thing.
 “What we showed in the last period against Buffalo, I thought we did a lot last year,” Tocchet said. “There was a lot of buy-in. We got pucks to the net. To me, it was just a textbook way we have to play.
 “Integrating other guys, you’re getting veteran guys back. Some of the young guys are pushing for jobs here. That’s a good thing. Internal competition makes your team better. It might push some people for urgency.”
 Having players such as Bonk and Knuble developing somewhat ahead of schedule can be a positive for the organization, both now and the near future.
 “Last year for the young guys [Porter Martone, Denver Barkey, Alex Bump] when they came up near the end of the year, those games are pressure games.
 “You look at Cole, [it’s] a nine-game losing streak, he gets called up – he’s playing in certain tough situations, like the last couple minutes of a game – and he did really well.”
 You get the impression Tocchet is keeping a close eye on these early 20s guys and imagining what this team will look like in a couple years.
 “You’re seeing guys in pressure situations and not in ideal [circumstances], like he [Knuble] is coming up when we’ve won seven in a row,” the coach said. “These guys are coming up when things aren’t great. I give them a lot of credit to interject life in our team.”
 The key here is finding a balance. As general manager Daniel Briere said last year, the plan is to not only succeed now but in the years to come.
 Tocchet confirms he will have a role in deciding how this potential “crowded elevator” jam of players actually plays out.
 “Like I said, Bonker, McDonald, [Ty] Murchison, [Spencer] Gill … they’re pushin’ to get on the big club,” Tocchet said. “It’s urgency time for people. I went through it as a player. When I was an older guy here, [Simon] Gagne, [Justin] Williams, they’re pushing your job.
 “It’s a good thing because there’s urgency. As I said, internal competition is good.”
 Wayne Fish is a freelance writer. Follow his coverage at www.flyingfishhockey.com
